name: Pataka
meaning: a flag, or signals stopping, blessing, or royal command
description: Formed by straightening all fingers close together while bending the thumb slightly inward. Represents victory, banners, divinity, or an authoritative command.
usage: Used by heroic Paccha characters like Arjuna or Rama to signal resolve or by divine beings conferring blessings.

name: Mudrakhya
meaning: indicates a ring, jewel, circular object, or subtle whisper
description: Formed by joining the tips of the index finger and thumb together with other fingers extended straight.
usage: Depicts signet rings, coins, small precious objects, or whispering secrets into a confidant's ear.

name: Kataka
meaning: holding something delicately, like a fresh flower, reins, or necklace
description: The middle finger and index finger bend toward the thumb while the ring and little fingers curve naturally.
usage: Depicts holding celestial flowers, arrows, reins of war chariots, or feminine adornments.

name: Mushti
meaning: a closed fist — firmness, holding tight, defiance, or grasping a weapon
description: All four fingers curled into the palm with the thumb pressed firmly across them.
usage: Demonstrates martial valor, striking blows, grasping maces or swords, or resolute defiance.

name: Kartarimukha
meaning: scissors or arrow — represents separation, opposition, or swift travel
description: Index and middle fingers extended apart in a V-shape like scissor blades, while the thumb touches the ring and little fingers.
usage: Signifies estrangement between lovers, lightning, paths crossing, or cutting bonds.

name: Sukatunda
meaning: a parrot's beak — denotes mystery, secret thoughts, or piercing darts
description: The ring finger bent at the knuckle resembling a hooked beak while other fingers are curved softly.
usage: Used in scenes of intrigue, romantic teasing, casting mystic darts, or secret inquiries.

name: Kappitthaka
meaning: holding sacred fruits, offering milk, or performing an invocation
description: Thumb pressed against the middle finger while the index bends over the thumb.
usage: Associated with offering ritual oblations, gathering wild woodland fruits, or holding sacred vessels.

name: Hamsapaksha
meaning: a swan's wing — flight, spreading waters, gentle breeze, or vast expanse
description: The little finger raised gracefully while the other three fingers extend flat with the thumb folded.
usage: Depicts gliding across lakes, wind whispering through canopy trees, or ocean waves.

name: Sikhara
meaning: a mountain peak, raising a bow, or expressing a question or argument
description: All fingers closed into a fist with the thumb pointed straight upward like a mountain spire.
usage: Portrays mighty summits of Gandhamadana, stringing the Gandiva bow, or challenging an adversary.

name: Hamsasyam
meaning: a swan's beak — denotes softness, plucking pearls, or delicate painting
description: Thumb, index, and middle fingertips joined closely while the other two fingers spread gently.
usage: Depicts picking jasmine blossoms, touching sacred drops of sandal paste, or tying ornamental silks.

name: Anjali
meaning: a respectful salutation, reverent offering, or heartfelt prayer
description: Palms or fingers brought together in gentle reverence before the chest, throat, or forehead.
usage: Offered to preceptors, elder brothers, deities, or as humble supplication before kings.

name: Ardhachandra
meaning: the crescent moon, receiving grace, or meditative stillness
description: Fingers held straight with the thumb stretched widely out to form a luminous crescent curve.
usage: Evokes nocturnal skies, the crescent on Shiva's crown, or holding sacred holy water.

name: Mukura
meaning: a mirror — self-reflection, beauty, vanity, or luminous countenance
description: The little finger and thumb raised straight up while middle fingers fold toward the palm.
usage: Heroines inspecting their adornments, admiring grace, or characters gazing into reflections.

name: Bhramara
meaning: a buzzing bee — hover over flower nectar, or whisper a secret
description: Index finger bent with the thumb touching the middle finger tip while remaining fingers fan out.
usage: Portrays spring blossoms, pollinators darting in groves, or stealthy movements.

name: Suchimukha
meaning: a sharp needle — pinpointing direction, expressing 'one', or piercing truth
description: Index finger extended straight up while all other fingers curl into the thumb.
usage: Pointing toward destiny, indicating singular determination, or tracing fine inscriptions.

name: Pallava
meaning: a tender sprout or young leaf — denotes gentleness, spring, and vitality
description: Fingers extended in a loose, graceful cascade resembling young shoots swaying in breeze.
usage: Denotes tender affection, spring breeze rustling leaves, or the blossoming of young love.

name: Tripataka
meaning: a three-coloured flag, towering tree, crown, or joyful affirmation
description: Pataka gesture with the third finger (ring finger) bent down sharply.
usage: Depicts grand trees in royal forests, sacred crowns, Indra's thunderbolt, or affirming 'yes'.

name: Mrigasirsha
meaning: a deer's head — roaming wildlife, gentle fear, or timid innocence
description: Thumb and little finger extended upward while index, middle, and ring fingers bend forward.
usage: Denotes innocent forest creatures, timid maidens wandering, or seeking solace in wilderness.

name: Sarpasira
meaning: a serpent's hood — venom, slithering creepers, or latent danger
description: All fingers curved inward into a hollow cupped shape mimicking a cobra's expanded hood.
usage: Depicts deadly serpents, poisonous draughts, subterranean realms, or insidious deceit.

name: Vardhamanaka
meaning: growth and expansion — a budding seedling or flourishing fortune
description: Fingers folded and uncurling progressively outward from the thumb.
usage: Signals increasing prosperity, ripening grain, or an unfolding epic narrative.

name: Arala
meaning: a bent curve — drinking poison, violent storms, or turbulent winds
description: Index finger curved like a bow while the thumb presses against its base.
usage: Portrays drinking the Kalakuta poison, turbulent mountain gales, or heroic exertion.

name: Urnanabha
meaning: a spider's claw or demonic grip — ferocity, tearing, or supernatural beasts
description: All five fingers separated widely and bent like sharp talons.
usage: Used by demonic Thadi or Kari characters like Dussasana or Surpanakha during terrifying combat.

name: Mukula
meaning: an unopened flower bud, water lily, or the act of feeding
description: All five fingertips brought tightly together in a point like an unopened lotus bud.
usage: Depicts closed lotuses at sunset, offering morsels, or modesty.

name: Katakamugha
meaning: stringing a war bow, releasing arrows, or adorning a garland
description: Index and middle fingers closed over the thumb with ring and little fingers extended outward.
usage: Depicts archers drawing bows to their ears, shooting divine astras, or clasping battle standards.
